name: Jalapeno Popper Chicken Casserole

ingredients.buy: 1 1/3 cups shredded cheddar, divided (most in the mix, the rest on top)
1 1/3 cups real bacon crumbles, divided (most stirred in, the rest on top)
about 11 jalapenos, seeded (most diced into the mix, a couple sliced for the top)

prose.intro_html: A jalapeno popper is a wonderful thing wrapped in a bad habit, all cream cheese and bacon and heat riding on a fried shell or a carb-heavy crumb. This casserole keeps the good part and throws out the shell. Tender chicken gets folded into a popper filling built for real, cream cheese loosened with mayo and sour cream, sharp cheddar, real bacon, and seeded jalapenos for warmth without the burn. It bakes under one more layer of cheddar and bacon with a few jalapeno slices on top until the whole dish bubbles. No breading, no fried anything, no flour. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 5 grams of carbs. That is the appetizer you love, turned into a dinner that works for your body and your wallet.
shop_smart: Three and a half pounds of chicken breast is the anchor. Cook it and chop it into bite-sized pieces to fold through the bake. Reach for the big family pack of boneless skinless breasts instead of the little trays, because you are paying for chicken, not packaging. This is where most of the protein and most of the money in the dish live.

Cream cheese, mayo, and sour cream are the popper. A fourteen ounce measure of softened cream cheese loosened with about three quarters of a cup each of mayo and sour cream is what makes a bite taste like the inside of a popper instead of a dry chicken bake. Buy the full-fat versions. This is a low-carb, calorie-honest dinner, and the light tubs would quietly drop it below where it is meant to land.

Cheddar and bacon each show up twice, so buy for both jobs. You want about a cup and a third of shredded cheddar and a cup and a third of real bacon crumbles, each divided, most stirred into the filling and the rest blanketing the top. Sharp cheddar pays you back in flavor, and real crumbled bacon carries the smoke that names the dish.

About eleven jalapenos bring the heat, and seeding them controls it. Cut them open and scrape the seeds and white ribs out, then dice most of them into the filling and thinly slice a couple for the top. That is where the burn hides, so seeded peppers give you steady warmth instead of a surprise. Want it milder still, swap in poblanos, which the source offers and cook the same way.

Garlic powder, salt, and pepper are the whole spice list. A couple of teaspoons of garlic powder with a little salt and black pepper is all the seasoning this needs, because the cream cheese, bacon, and peppers are already doing the loud work. Nothing exotic to hunt down.
make_it: Weigh your empty baking dish and write the number down. You will need it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight, which is the only honest way to portion one big bake.

Heat the oven to 350 degrees F and grease a large baking dish. If your chicken is not already cooked, poach or roast it now, then chop it and set it aside. Seed the jalapenos, dice most of them, and thinly slice a couple for the top.
In a large bowl, beat the softened cream cheese with the mayo and sour cream until smooth. Stir in the garlic powder, salt, and black pepper.
Fold in the chopped chicken, most of the cheddar, most of the bacon, and the diced jalapenos, holding back a handful of cheddar and bacon for the top. Mix until everything is evenly coated.
Spread the mixture level in the baking dish. Scatter the reserved cheddar and bacon over the top, then lay the sliced jalapenos across it.

Bake at 350 degrees F for about 35 minutes, until the top is melted and the casserole is hot and bubbling. A deeper 14-serving dish may want a few extra minutes, so go by the bubble, not just the clock.
Let it rest a few minutes so it firms up, then weigh the dish, subtract the empty weight from Step 1, and divide across 14 containers.
prose.portion_html: Set the baked dish on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the total. Divide that number by 14 and scoop that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a baked, bubbling jalapeno popper casserole that eats like the appetizer and skips the breading. The chicken and the cheese carry it; the peppers and bacon do the flavor the fried shell used to, for a lot less.

steps: Weigh the empty baking dish and note the number for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 350 degrees F, cook and chop the chicken if needed, and seed and cut the jalapenos.
Beat the softened cream cheese with the mayo and sour cream until smooth, then season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Fold in the chicken, most of the cheddar, most of the bacon, and the diced jalapenos.
Spread in the dish, top with the reserved cheddar and bacon, and lay the sliced jalapenos on top.
Bake at 350 degrees F for about 35 minutes until bubbling, going by the bubble on a deeper dish.
Rest, then weigh the dish and divide across 14 containers.
